description: We are Lunar G-Spotters, combining aerospace engineering and a passion for lunar exploration. Our project, SELENE, uses NASA data to explore how location, time and terrain affect Sun and Earth visibility from the Moon. Join us to build an interactive, scientifically grounded tool. We welcome skills in software development, UI/UX, planetary science, data visualisation and storytelling.
summary: SELENE helps planners and scientists explore a critical lunar question: what changes when a landing location, date, or horizon changes? Designed for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, SELENE transforms NASA/JPL Horizons Sun and Earth ephemerides into topocentric sky views, visibility timelines, and saved scenario comparisons. A terrain rehearsal feature uses NASA LRO LOLA elevation data to identify exact blocking ridges limiting lines of sight, directly connecting visibility numbers to local topography. Users can inspect assumptions, compare alternatives, and preserve evidence. SELENE provides rapid engineering exploration and education; results are inspectable geometric screening estimates rather than certified power or communication predictions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Near the lunar south pole, low solar elevations and variable Earth visibility make site selection and operational timing critical. A small schedule adjustment can dramatically change sunlight or direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication. SELENE brings disparate ephemeris and elevation datasets into an integrated, interactive workflow.

A curated Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) mission atlas displays published coordinates for landed missions (IM-1, IM-2, Blue Ghost 1) on an interactive 3D lunar globe. Users can request topocentric observations for any coordinate and UTC window, or explore offline using bundled NASA datasets.

The platform calculates apparent airless Sun and Earth elevations, tracks visible arcs across a 360-degree local sky dome, and determines joint visibility durations and outage brackets. Users can perform parametric sweeps across uniform horizon obstructions and clearance margins.

For coordinates within the retained south-polar Digital Elevation Model (DEM), a terrain analysis computes real skylines along 360 one-degree azimuth rays out to 100 km. The 3D Terrain Rehearsal reconstructs a 38.4 km local patch, allowing users to select a bearing, inspect the limiting blocker ridge, and follow Sun/Earth tracks along the shared observation clock.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Rather than presenting static animations, SELENE keeps scientific reasoning completely inspectable. For example, at 89.5° S, 0° E over November 2026, a flat horizon yields 364 hours of joint Sun and Earth visibility; incorporating real LOLA terrain reveals that local ridges reduce this window to 134 hours and extend Earth blackout to 392 hours. SELENE enables early-stage concept teams to rapidly evaluate trade-offs and serves as an educational tool explaining lunar celestial geometry.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

- Languages & Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and CSS3.

- 3D & 2D Graphics: Three.js (r186.1) for the lunar globe and 3D terrain rehearsal; HTML5 Canvas for topocentric sky domes and orbital tracking.

- Backend & Processing: Node.js standard-library local server for Horizons ephemeris proxying and worker-thread LOLA raycasting; Python standard library for independent validation.

- Standalone Edition: A zero-dependency 23 MB single-file HTML build (SELENE.html) with embedded textures and precomputed terrain for full offline use.

CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED

SELENE bridges macro-scale celestial mechanics with micro-scale surface topography. It balances high visual polish with strict scientific transparency: angles are apparent airless body-center directions, durations strictly obey interval-start weighting without fabricated crossing interpolations, and all data transfers (.selene.json) preserve source provenance.
